name: How do I know if my pool coping is failing?

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my pool coping is failing?
mainEntity.text: How do I know if my pool coping is failing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pool coping is failing when it shows movement, cracking, separation, or repeated grout or sealant failure. Loose sections, hollow sounds, sharp edges, and gaps where the coping meets the deck are all warning signs. Water intrusion and recurring staining around the waterline can also point to a bigger issue. Coping problems matter because they affect both appearance and waterproofing. If the coping is allowing water behind the finish, a simple cosmetic patch may not be enough. In many remodels, coping replacement is bundled with tile and resurfacing because the perimeter area is where several problems meet at once. Homeowners should have the coping inspected before choosing finishes, especially if the pool is older or if the deck has settled. If the contractor says the coping can be reused, ask how it was tested and whether the surrounding waterproofing is still sound. Replacing failing coping during the remodel is usually safer than waiting until after new finishes are installed.
acceptedAnswer.description: Failing coping often shows visible cracks, loose stones, hollow spots, separation from the deck, water intrusion, or sharp edges. If coping moves when pressed or has recurring grout failure, it may need replacement rather than repair. Coping problems can also signal waterproofing or settlement issues.
